traditions.r: Mongolia, Central Asia and the Caucasus
traditions.p: Nomadic pastoral tradition; dried yoghurt recorded in Arabic cookbooks from the 10th century
traditions.d: Pastoral dairy foods (tsagaan idee) eaten fresh in summer and dried into curd and yoghurt balls for winter.
traditions.tech: Churning yoghurt to remove butter, boiling and draining buttermilk curd, shaping and sun-drying for weeks
traditions.mat: Cow, yak, sheep, goat or mare's milk; salt
traditions.auth: Sun-dried, hand-shaped pieces with texture varying by animal; traditional qurut made from churned buttermilk rather than oven-fermented yoghurt.

traditions.r: Nepal, Bhutan, Tibet and Northeast India
traditions.d: Mountain cheesemaking from yak and cow buttermilk, producing soft fresh chhurpi and fire-dried hard chewing cheese.
traditions.tech: Buttermilk boiled, curd drained in cloth, pressed in jute bags, cut into cubes and dried over a fire
traditions.auth: Hard chhurpi is extremely hard and lasts 30 minutes to five hours in the mouth; soft chhurpi is white and mild.

notes: 5 kinds, 15 archetypes, 0 brands, 2 traditions. Qurut (k91) and Jameed (k92) merged into 'Qurut & jameed' with Chortan as a third archetype; Aaruul's old model 'Aarts' became an archetype and Eezgii was added. Kashk now has Iranian, Turkish, Levantine and Egyptian archetypes. Old sources (retail store, Czech blog, nenow, List_of_dairy_products) were replaced by retrieved Wikipedia/ANU pages; en.wikipedia Qurut, Jameed and Aaruul all redirect to the Kashk article. Left out: brand Kashk Hendessi (the Wikipedia claim is marked citation needed); the mansaf/Karak association for jameed and the Rubing link for rushan (no retrieved page confirms them); dates for each archetype other than kashk.
